newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL dodges around French trucking dispute.
newsitem.headline: DHL dodges around French trucking dispute.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it had made contingency plans for its road services in response to industrial action by French lorry drivers.

"Yesterday evening we cancelled our scheduled trucking services between Brussels and Paris because of road blocks on the A1 motorway and put on a 20-tonne Boeing 727F round-trip in its place," a Brussels-based DHL official told Reuters.
DHL would be taking a decision later today on whether to maintain the Brussels-Paris/CDG-Brussels contingency flight this evening.

"Elsewhere, our air cargo line-haul services from Brussels to French provincial cities - Nantes, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Marseille, Nice and Lyon, are operating as normal," the official said. Final delivery is by DHL vehicles operating from the regional French airports.
The two sides in the dispute are scheduled to resume negotiations at 15.00 hrs local (14.00 GMT) Tuesday.
If the lorry drivers dispute was prolonged there could be a problem with aircraft fuel supplies In France, the official added.
"We are putting in more fuel than usual at Brussels instead of running the risk of not being able to re-fuel at French airports en route and this can have an impact on pay loads."

At Bordeaux, DHL is having to cope with a lack of diesel in the region to run its fleet of vans and small trucks. "It's becoming very difficult to find fuel but our pick-up and distribution services are continuing for the moment," a Bordeaux-based DHL official said.
DHL's Bordeaux centre had recorded a strong increase in its normal traffic volumes since the lorry drivers dispute started.

"Shippers and forwarders have decided that road transport constitutes too much of a risk at present and have turned to air cargo as an alternative," the official added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
